properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-31. Nothing chosen.

⭐⭐ READ THE HAZARD FIRST — THIS EXACT QUESTION HAS ALREADY MISFIRED TWICE ON STALE RECORDS. On 2026-08-23 an agent asked where else to optimise, read `fact:the-orientation-reads-cost-ten-seconds-and-the-store-is-not-why`, and quoted three claims back as current that PR #290 had already made false. Anthony corrected it — "I think we already determined candidate 3" — and he was right while the graph was wrong. That incident is why `req:the-graph-can-say-what-has-already-been-done` exists. It happened AGAIN on 2026-08-31, this session, on the parallel-batch finding. Any sweep that starts by reading old findings will reproduce it a third time.

THE WINS ALREADY TAKEN, so nobody re-derives them:
    hydrate to queryable      8,828 ms -> 909 ms
    build_export_doc          1,137 ms -> 237 ms
    detect_structural_defects  44.5 s  -> 4.43 s
    open_questions (1st call)  11.7 s  -> 2.95 s   (56 SPOF candidates: 878 ms each -> 5.08 ms for all 56)

TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT ARE STILL LIVE AND UNCLOSED, which is where a fresh look would start:
· THE LIVE STORE CARRIES 7.4x THE BYTES OF ITS OWN CONTENT (`fact:every-cost-number-today-was-a-debug-build-and-the-live-store-is-7x-its-content`). That is a compaction/GC question nobody has taken.
· THE BUILD PROFILE IS WORTH 2.2x ON `loop_status` — so part of what feels slow to a developer is debug-vs-release rather than code, and any new number must say which profile it was taken in.

⚠️ THE DISCIPLINE IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND CI ENFORCES IT. The `optimize` skill requires the budget to precede the code, the number to be DERIVED rather than picked, measurement against the budget rather than the starting point, stopping when it is met, recording what was deliberately left undone, and it explicitly ALLOWS the answer "nothing here". So "identify areas where we can improve performance" has a prescribed shape: name the target and the budget first, or do not start.

OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS: what is the target — a user-visible latency, a CI wall-clock, a memory ceiling? Whose experience is being improved, Alex's session or a developer's build? And is 7.4x store overhead actually costing anyone anything, or is it merely untidy?
properties.name: OPEN — is there performance left worth taking after the four big wins, and what budget would say when it is done?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm discipline. The wins-already-taken table is included deliberately and is the most load-bearing part of this node: the recorded failure mode for this specific question is a session re-deriving closed work from a stale finding, twice now.
